newsitem.title: UK: Improving harvest ideas push LIFFE wheat lower.
newsitem.headline: Improving harvest ideas push LIFFE wheat lower.

text.p: LIFFE wheat fell as the new crop was hit by sentiment that the UK is heading for a big harvest, traders said.
Old crop, seen as still abundant, fell more sharply.
November was most active, with 372 of a total 616 lots done. It last traded 0.65 stg lower, at 88.50 stg.
July fell by 1.70 to 79.50 stg. One trader, noting that this was July's first foray into the seventies, described the nine stg discount against November as "amazing."
"There were a lot of sellers. The whole country has been selling into us," he said, referring to the futures market.
But the futures fall meant a sidelined physical market. "The futures are down so people are just backing off," one delivered market broker said. "It's come off with a wallop," another said.

Brokers reported milling wheat done for delivery to the west of England at 111.00 stg for June and 112.50 stg for July. Feed Wheat was done to Norfolk/Suffolk at 83.00 stg for June and 84.50 stg for July.
